item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nitrogen is essential in agricultural fertilizers, yet its nanoscale interfacial dynamics remain largely unexplored. Although quadrupolar broadening complicates $^{14}$N nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) detection, $^{15}$N (I=1/2) provides well-defined nuclear-spin signatures but remains challenging to detect at the nanoscale due to its low natural abundance and small gyromagnetic ratio. Here, we use a microfluidic quantum sensing platform based on shallow nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond to detect $^{15}$N NMR from KNO$_{3}$ solution at room temperature and in a low magnetic field regime. Within femtoliter-scale sensing volumes, we measure a magnetic-field variance of up to ~442 nT$^{2}$, ~43 times greater than the expected statistical polarization. The $^{15}$N spin correlation decays within ~500 $\mu\mathrm{s}$, mainly limited by the NV spin lattice relaxation time and not by the molecular diffusion of the KNO$_{3}$ molecules. This is consistent with the formation of a KNO$_{3}$ adsorption layer on the diamond surface, supported by surface characterization.

item.title: Constructively Embedding Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.33389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Implementing quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs) requires more than favorable algebraic parameters: the interactions among data qubits and ancillas must also fit physical hardware. Surface codes map naturally onto two-dimensional…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Implementing quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs) requires more than favorable algebraic parameters: the interactions among data qubits and ancillas must also fit physical hardware. Surface codes map naturally onto two-dimensional arrays, but many quantum LDPC codes have Tanner graphs with nonlocal connections. We develop a constructive pipeline that maps a QECC's Tanner graph to the targeted hardware lattice in three stages (continuous embedding, grid assignment, and path routing). Continuous embeddings reveal the geometric structure of the code, including differences between stabilizer generator sets of the same code. The discrete stages produce explicit routed layouts that we can characterize and compare using proxy metrics for footprint, communication overhead, and congestion for syndrome extraction. We examine three continuous embedding methods: multidimensional scaling (distance-based), spectral embedding (Laplacian-based), and spring layout (force-based) for the first stage. Experiments across tested codes show how routing geometry, dimension, and scale selection affect the resulting costs. In ablation studies on the radius-2 (R2) HaPPY code, graph-aware methods for continuous embedding and the choice of path-routing algorithm matter more than the grid assignment under our chosen weights in the cost function. Changing the continuous embedding reveals a trade-off: MDS incurs greater communication overhead than spectral embedding over most tested scales, while spring layout can reduce communication overhead at intermediate scales but increases congestion and is less stable across scales.

item.title: How Many Keys Must a Quantum Computer Break to Take Over a Blockchain? A Quantum Nakamoto Coefficient for Fifteen Proof-of-Stake Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.33413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blockchains that run on proof of stake, among them Ethereum and Solana, are secured by a vote: a transaction becomes irreversible once computers holding two thirds of the deposited money have signed it. Each signature is made with a…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blockchains that run on proof of stake, among them Ethereum and Solana, are secured by a vote: a transaction becomes irreversible once computers holding two thirds of the deposited money have signed it. Each signature is made with a secret key whose public counterpart is permanently visible, and a large quantum computer could compute the secret from the public key. We ask a simple question: how many such keys would it have to break to take over the vote? We call the answer the quantum Nakamoto coefficient and measure it on live data from fifteen networks, collected on 15 November 2026. For fourteen of them, 2 to 18 keys are enough to break the network's security guarantee and 7 to 77 to control it outright; at one key every 12 minutes, the pace implied by recent resource estimates, a single quantum computer would defeat the guarantee of any of these networks in less than four hours and take full control in less than sixteen hours. Ethereum is far more robust, but a 2025 change that lets operators merge their deposits into fewer keys has cut the number of keys at its first threshold from about 465,000 to 7,682, a factor of 60. We derive a simple formula for this effect, and another for the small rotating committee on which wallets rely, and confirm both on the data. For fourteen of the fifteen networks, the first large quantum computer would be less than a day away from total control. Their validator signatures should therefore be migrated to post-quantum schemes before such a machine exists, since once it does, the time to respond is measured in hours.

item.title: Extracting Operational Entanglement from a Noise-Protected Many-Body System
item.description: arXiv:2611.33421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can noisy dynamics generate entanglement that stays useful at long times? Under collective dephasing, a twelve-spin kicked Ising ring evolves from a uniform product state toward an entangled stationary state that is maximally mixed …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can noisy dynamics generate entanglement that stays useful at long times? Under collective dephasing, a twelve-spin kicked Ising ring evolves from a uniform product state toward an entangled stationary state that is maximally mixed in the sector fixed by the ring's rotations and reflections. Gates and measurements within each half herald a spin pair that teleports an unknown qubit with a mean fidelity of 90.5\%. Simulations show that stronger noise correlations extend the time over which the ring yields pairs that beat the classical teleportation limit.

item.title: Estimating the Trotter error via phase analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.33438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Good Trotter error estimates are crucial to correctly assess the resources required to perform an approximate time evolution with a target accuracy. General bounds for finite-size quantum systems are found to be very loose in practi…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Good Trotter error estimates are crucial to correctly assess the resources required to perform an approximate time evolution with a target accuracy. General bounds for finite-size quantum systems are found to be very loose in practice, and it is therefore highly desirable to improve on them. In this work, we analyze the Trotter error in terms of the spectrum of a phase operator that we construct from the Hamiltonian. In the limit of a small Trotter step size, we obtain an estimate of the Trotter error written in terms of a sum of nested commutators between terms of the Hamiltonian. The structure of this estimate allows us to naturally explain the looseness of general bounds. We show that even for a finite step size, our estimate typically remains more accurate than general bounds. Moreover, we argue that it becomes an upper bound for the Trotter error per step in the limit of a large number of steps, reflecting the destructive interference of the errors across steps. Our results provide useful practical heuristics for resource optimization in quantum simulations.

item.title: A Realistic End-to-End Runtime Crossover Estimation for Quantum-Enhanced Training of Large-Scale Machine Learning Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.33454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine Learning (ML) is one promising application domain for Quantum Computing (QC) speedups, but asymptotic complexity considerations often mask the actual engineering costs of actual end-to-end workflows. For the use case of trai…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine Learning (ML) is one promising application domain for Quantum Computing (QC) speedups, but asymptotic complexity considerations often mask the actual engineering costs of actual end-to-end workflows. For the use case of training a linearized Neural Network with a Quantum Linear Solver, a provably favorable quantum scaling has been suggested. We present realistic resource estimates for this problem, accounting for data access, computation, and readout. Our analysis examines three increasingly complex benchmarking scenarios, under distinct sparsity-scaling assumptions, thereby enabling progressively more realistic resource estimates. We identify crossover regimes relative to classical methods and find that crossover points emerge only for very large problem sizes, long computation times, and highly restrictive output requirements. This work provides a blueprint for evaluating quantum-enhanced ML algorithms under realistic hardware constraints and help identifying the bottlenecks that must be overcome to approach industrial quantum utility.

item.title: NISQ Preparation of Conditional Thermal States for Precision Thermometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.33461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ability to prepare thermal states on gate-based quantum computers is an important building block for quantum computation, both with regard to the implementation of certain classes of quantum algorithms as well as to the study of…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ability to prepare thermal states on gate-based quantum computers is an important building block for quantum computation, both with regard to the implementation of certain classes of quantum algorithms as well as to the study of quantum thermodynamics in and out of equilibrium. A useful generalization of the standard notion of a thermal state which appears naturally in the study of quantum work distributions is the conditional thermal state, which is conditioned on the use of an accessible pointer basis associated with a measurement apparatus. Among other uses, it has been proven that conditional thermal states can outperform ordinary thermal states in quantum thermometry. In this work we demonstrate the preparation of conditional thermal states of few-qubit systems implemented on IonQ's cloud-based quantum computers across a range of temperatures. To validate their performance advantage in thermometry, we measure the sub-quantum Fisher information (a lower bound on the quantum Fisher information) of the prepared states, which can be computed via a constant-depth quantum circuit without tomography.

item.title: Optimal Controlled Quantum Instrument for Monitored Many-Body Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.33472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-selecting rare trajectories of monitored quantum dynamics requires exponentially many repeated experiments. We extend Bayes' rule to monitored many-body dynamics and bias the quantum trajectories by nonlinear functions of the p…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-selecting rare trajectories of monitored quantum dynamics requires exponentially many repeated experiments. We extend Bayes' rule to monitored many-body dynamics and bias the quantum trajectories by nonlinear functions of the post-measurement state. For functions that are constant on the sets of a suitable finite partition of the post-measurement states, we construct a quantum instrument on the system and an additional register that produces the biased trajectories at the optimal rates without post-selection. This optimal controlled quantum instrument has a natural tensor-network representation as the left canonical form of the system--register tensors. We illustrate the construction with two examples: a precessing qubit, biased by its spin component along the field, and free fermions with gain and loss, biased by the particle number, where the biased trajectories undergo a phase transition. We also argue, under one assumption, that biasing a measured Majorana chain by its von Neumann entropy leads to entanglement transitions.

item.title: Infrared-absorption magnetometry in a diamond nanocavity: demonstration and limits at the nanoscale
item.description: arXiv:2611.33481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diamond quantum sensors promise both high spatial resolution and high sensitivity; however, conventional photoluminescence-based spin readout can be difficult to integrate efficiently. Infrared absorption by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) ce…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diamond quantum sensors promise both high spatial resolution and high sensitivity; however, conventional photoluminescence-based spin readout can be difficult to integrate efficiently. Infrared absorption by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond provides a promising alternative, although the sensitivity of compact absorption-based sensors is limited by the short optical interaction length between the probe field and the NV ensemble. To overcome this limitation, we demonstrate, for the first time, singlet-absorption magnetometry using spin-dense diamond nanocavities. By probing cavity modes near the 1042 nm NV singlet transition, we observe spin-dependent cavity transmission and perform cavity-enhanced magnetic field sensing. We further develop and experimentally validate a model that accurately predicts the spin-dependent cavity response, describes the optimal operating conditions, and identifies the practical limitations of different optically detected magnetic resonance modalities. Together, these results establish cavity-enhanced singlet absorption as a scalable readout mechanism for integrated diamond quantum sensors and provide a practical framework for engineering next-generation nanophotonic diamond quantum magnetometers.

item.title: Reducing T gates in product formulas with agent loops
item.description: arXiv:2611.33509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum chemistry calculations on a fault-tolerant quantum computer usually require many $\text{T}$ gates. This cost depends on the simulation method and how precisely its rotations are implemented. In this paper, we used Nemotron 3…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum chemistry calculations on a fault-tolerant quantum computer usually require many $\text{T}$ gates. This cost depends on the simulation method and how precisely its rotations are implemented. In this paper, we used Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a large language model (LLM), in a coding-agent loop to optimize the structure and rotation-synthesis precision of product formulas (PFs) for quantum phase estimation (QPE). Each of five independent searches optimized a shared protocol across 115 HamLib molecular Hamiltonians spanning 4--16 qubits over 100 code mutations. The searches started from a calibrated, nested second-order PF with uniform synthesis precision. We minimized $T_{95}$, the estimated total $\text{T}$-gate cost including QPE queries and repeated attempts for $95\%$ success probability, while requiring chemical accuracy for every training Hamiltonian. We name the best protocol found error-limited optimized Trotter evolution (ELOTE). It achieves chemical accuracy for its training data and achieved median and geometric-mean $T_{95}$ reductions of $85.35\%$ and $84.82\%$, respectively. ELOTE combines contributions to the same Pauli string, uses a first-order PF, and varies synthesis precision with coefficient magnitude, Pauli support, and diagonal character. We also tested ELOTE on 76 larger Hamiltonians with 18--22 qubits, which met chemical accuracy in every case. For ten reaction energies, we further optimized a shared $\delta$-ELOTE protocol. It reduced geometric-mean $T_{95}$ by $58.90\%$ relative to ELOTE while preserving chemical accuracy for every signed reaction difference. These classically verified results show cost savings from shared protocols across molecules and reactions, and motivate similar searches in which energy measurements from quantum computers guide explorations in a coding-agent loop.

item.title: Robust Certification of Non-projective Qubit Measurements without Inputs
item.description: arXiv:2611.33559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) beyond projective simulation (aka non-projective measurements) offer advantages over projective measurements, motivating their certification directly from observed statistics. Here, we show …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) beyond projective simulation (aka non-projective measurements) offer advantages over projective measurements, motivating their certification directly from observed statistics. Here, we show that this certification can be achieved robustly without input randomness, using only the joint outcome distribution of two measurement devices. We consider two spatially separated observers whose only shared resource is an uncharacterised two-qubit state. Each observer performs a local measurement. In the projective-simulable case, the measurement device privately randomises over qubit projective measurements and applies arbitrary classical post-processing to their outcomes. In the noiseless regime, we identify three- and four-outcome anti-correlations that certify that both local measurements lie beyond projective simulation. To establish noise robustness, we develop a non-linear covariance witness that combines the geometry of projective measurements with a contraction bound valid for every two-qubit state. For the correlations generated by identical qubit trine measurements or identical qubit SIC-POVM on noisy qubit singlet, we obtain exact critical white-noise fractions of (1/4) and (1/3), respectively. Below these thresholds, no pair of projective-simulable measurements on any two-qubit state can reproduce these correlations. We present explicit projective simulations that attain the thresholds and cover the remaining noise range. Finally, the same method yields a strictly positive noise tolerance for certification whenever both observers apply the same extremal qubit POVM with three or four non-zero effects to a depolarised qubit singlet. These results establish a general analytic framework for certifying non-projective qubit measurement resources without input randomness.

item.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
item.description: arXiv:2611.33590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibil…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing technologies, and demonstrated high-fidelity operations. However, realizing a scalable architecture that supports quantum error correction, qubit transport, wiring, and logical gate operations remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scalable dense silicon spin qubit architecture designed to support large-scale FTQC. The architecture consists of qubit memories, data qubit lanes, and cross junctions. Qubit memories store logical qubits encoded using the rotated surface code and support logical single-qubit operations. Data qubit lanes enable high-speed one-dimensional spin shuttling for connectivity between logical qubits, while cross junctions provide routing functionality and implement transversal logical CNOT gates. Using experimentally demonstrated silicon spin qubit parameters, we evaluate logical error rates as a function of code distance and estimate that a code distance of at least 21 is required to achieve logical error rates below $10^{-10}$ per syndrome cycle. We further analyze wiring constraints based on CMOS-compatible multiplexed control schemes and show that, with optimized wiring efficiency, more than 120,000 logical qubits could be integrated on a 100 mm $\times$ 100 mm chip. These results provide a practical roadmap toward large-scale FTQC based on silicon spin qubit technology.

item.title: High-Dimensional Single-Photon Frequency Conversion for Orbital Angular Momentum Comb State
item.description: arXiv:2611.33642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The orbital angular momentum (OAM) degree of freedom provides an important resource for constructing high-dimensional optical quantum information systems. However, the generation of high-dimensional single-photon OAM comb state and …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The orbital angular momentum (OAM) degree of freedom provides an important resource for constructing high-dimensional optical quantum information systems. However, the generation of high-dimensional single-photon OAM comb state and its high-fidelity frequency conversion remain challenging due to limited spatial modulation resolution, imperfect mode matching, and finite nonlinear conversion efficiency. Here, we proposed and experimentally demonstrated a scalable scheme for the generation and frequency conversion of high-dimensional single-photon OAM comb state. We prepared a single-photon OAM comb state with a dimension of up to 128, achieving a fidelity of 0.787 between the reconstructed and target states and an effective dimension of 100. Furthermore, using the sum-frequency generation, we demonstrated the frequency upconversion of single-photon high-dimensional OAM comb state from the communication band to a visible wavelength of 520 nm, while verifying the preservation of both the OAM mode distribution and phase information through density matrix reconstruction. Our work established a versatile platform for the generation, manipulation, and characterization of high-dimensional OAM comb states, with potential applications in cross-band quantum information transfer, high-capacity quantum communication, and high-dimensional quantum networks.

item.title: Amatlas: A 2D Array Architecture for Union-Find Decoding Without Global Coordination
item.description: arXiv:2611.33665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-time decoding of the surface code is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, and scaling the decoder to large code distances in hardware remains a challenge. The locality of Union-Find (UF) decoding makes it a leading c…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-time decoding of the surface code is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, and scaling the decoder to large code distances in hardware remains a challenge. The locality of Union-Find (UF) decoding makes it a leading candidate for such a decoder in distributed hardware. Prior distributed UF decoders, however, map the three-dimensional decoding graph onto an array of processing elements (PEs) under a central controller that synchronizes all PEs at every stage, and a three-dimensional array of PEs scales poorly on planar hardware. This paper presents Amatlas, a two-dimensional PE array for UF decoding that operates without a central controller. Amatlas assigns one PE to each stabilizer on the two-dimensional qubit lattice and stores the states of all measurement rounds in the local memory of the PE, so every link connects adjacent PEs in the array. Every PE advances on every clock cycle without array-wide synchronization, and the clock is the only global signal of the array. Under circuit-level noise, the RTL implementation of Amatlas fits a VCU129 FPGA up to a code distance of 25, where the average decoding time is 462 ns per round at a physical error rate of 0.1%. Amatlas achieves a threshold of 0.72%, compared with 0.78% reported for UF decoding under the same noise model.

item.title: Dimensional crossover to a slow disordered spin bath below the mean spin spacing
item.description: arXiv:2611.33699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How thin must a layer of spins be to act as a two-dimensional bath? For nitrogen spins around an NV$^-$ centre in diamond, a cluster expansion with flip-flopping outer spins gives a crossover near the mean spin spacing. Thin layers …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How thin must a layer of spins be to act as a two-dimensional bath? For nitrogen spins around an NV$^-$ centre in diamond, a cluster expansion with flip-flopping outer spins gives a crossover near the mean spin spacing. Thin layers follow two-dimensional scaling with a prefactor six to seven times that of bulk. Without hyperfine disorder the crossover remains but the step is under three: the disorder leaves each spin almost no resonant partner. Flip-flops allow several milliseconds, so another process must set the measured 0.5 ms; nitrogen spin-lattice relaxation is consistent.

item.title: On-Demand Tailoring of High-Dimensional Orbital Angular Momentum States via a Phase-Only Hologram
item.description: arXiv:2611.33704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic orbital angular momentum (OAM) provides a naturally discrete and unbounded Hilbert space for high-dimensional encoding and has emerged as a powerful degree of freedom for advanced information processing. On-demand tailoring…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic orbital angular momentum (OAM) provides a naturally discrete and unbounded Hilbert space for high-dimensional encoding and has emerged as a powerful degree of freedom for advanced information processing. On-demand tailoring of both the amplitude and phase profiles of high-dimensional OAM states is essential for numerous applications, particularly in quantum information science. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate an efficient method for achieving such on-demand tailoring using a purely phase-only modulation scheme. The measured fidelity remains above 80% even for a 128-dimensional state, demonstrating the scalability of the approach. Compared with previous techniques, our method achieves significantly higher generation efficiency, and this advantage becomes more pronounced as the dimensionality increases. Moreover, our approach substantially reduces experimental complexity while maintaining precise control, thereby offering a practical and scalable solution for high-dimensional OAM state engineering in both classical and quantum information processing.

item.title: When Malus' Law Meets the Wigner-Bell Inequality: Violation by Nonseparable Classical Light
item.description: arXiv:2611.33729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bell-type inequalities are commonly associated with quantum nonlocality, yet their mathematical structure also reflects more general constraints on the joint probability distributions assigned to measurements performed in different …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bell-type inequalities are commonly associated with quantum nonlocality, yet their mathematical structure also reflects more general constraints on the joint probability distributions assigned to measurements performed in different contexts. Here we examine this distinction through the Wigner--Bell inequality using a classical optical field with two nonseparable degrees of freedom. Starting from a subsystem response-factorization assumption, we derive a Wigner-type probability bound requiring the pairwise measurement statistics to be compatible with a single nonnegative global joint distribution. For a classically nonseparable optical field, the corresponding joint probabilities are represented directly by normalized joint intensities and obey Malus' law. We show that these Malus-law probabilities violate the Wigner--Bell bound over a finite range of analyzer settings. The violation does not imply spatial nonlocality or a failure of classical electrodynamics. Rather, it demonstrates the incompatibility of context-dependent optical projection statistics with the global probability assignment underlying the Wigner construction. We further derive an extended Wigner-Bell bound for general imperfect correlations and propose an interferometric experiment for reconstructing the required joint probabilities from intensity measurements. These results provide a transparent optical realization of the probabilistic structure behind Bell-type inequalities and help distinguish consequences of Hilbert-space structure, nonseparability, and measurement context from those specifically associated with quantum nonlocality.

item.title: Improved Quantum Algorithms for TSP and More
item.description: arXiv:2611.33730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The traveling salesman problem (TSP) is a canonical NP-hard optimization problem. For general edge weights, the classical dynamic programs of Bellman and of Held and Karp solve TSP on $n$ cities in $O^*(2^n)$ time. To date, no $\Oh(…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The traveling salesman problem (TSP) is a canonical NP-hard optimization problem. For general edge weights, the classical dynamic programs of Bellman and of Held and Karp solve TSP on $n$ cities in $O^*(2^n)$ time. To date, no $\Oh(c^n)$-time classical algorithm is known for any $c<2$. Combining Grover search with the dynamic programming technique, Ambainis et al. (SODA 2019) introduced a quantum algorithm with running time $O^*(1.7274^n)$, which is still the best known quantum time bound. In this work, we improve the running time to $O^*(1.70961^n)$. The core idea of our algorithm is to combine the framework of Ambainis et al. with the extremal set-system framework, which was recently used for classical space-time tradeoffs of TSP by Jabal Ameli, Nederlof and Wang (FOCS 2026) and Dallant and Kozma (FOCS 2026). To obtain our upper bound, we decompose the optimal tour into four consecutive subpaths of different sizes, for which, based on the idea of set-systems, the optimal values are computed using dynamic programming with small success probability and use amplitude amplification. Using the same idea, we also give a new quantum space-time tradeoff for TSP, improving the previous results of Caroppo et al. (ESA 2026) and Dallant (arXiv:2607.12374). Finally, we obtain the same quantum upper bounds for several other related problems.

item.title: Structure theorem for quantum limit cycle attractors: A geometric path-integral approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.33776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show a Structure Theorem for an arbitrary separable quantum system (\(\dim\mathcal{H}\leq\aleph_0\)) that is coupled, through a symmetric bidirectional phase interface, to a self-sustaining phase-oscillator environment. Under the…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show a Structure Theorem for an arbitrary separable quantum system (\(\dim\mathcal{H}\leq\aleph_0\)) that is coupled, through a symmetric bidirectional phase interface, to a self-sustaining phase-oscillator environment. Under the assumptions of \(U(1)\) covariance, instantaneous Lindblad bounded positivity, and the existence of an entrainable periodic attractor, the reduced generator is forced into a universal operator structure consisting of a state-dependent coherent recoil together with single-quantum feedback. Positivity further imposes a sharp dimensional dichotomy: purely dissipative gain saturation is forbidden in finite dimensions by trace-norm contraction, so coherent feedback is mandatory for qubits and qudits, whereas unbounded ladder algebras permit purely dissipative saturation. Expanding the general feedback functionals to leading order in the coupling recovers a canonical polynomial master equation that remains completely positive and trace-preserving in every dimension and combines additively with ordinary linear Lindblad channels. An accompanying Inverse Coupling Theorem shows that an autonomous periodic orbit can be sustained only when the interaction manifold has non-trivial fundamental group \(\pi_1(\mathcal{M})=\mathbb{Z}\), thereby isolating the sinusoidal \(U(1)\)-covariant phase coupling as the generic mechanism. The resulting implementation is realized explicitly for a single qubit, a bipartite two-qubit system, and a bosonic Fock space.

item.title: QPAT: A Universal Quantum Machine Learning Framework for Quantum-Assisted Training and Classical Inference
item.description: arXiv:2611.33806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep learning models often struggle with sharp local optima and overfitting in limited-data regimes, and exhibit limited capacity for capturing high-order, complex probability distributions. Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models, by…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep learning models often struggle with sharp local optima and overfitting in limited-data regimes, and exhibit limited capacity for capturing high-order, complex probability distributions. Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models, by operating in exponentially large Hilbert spaces, can efficiently represent such distributions and provide favorable inductive biases for learning, offering a promising pathway to overcome these limitations. However, their practical deployment in the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era is severely hindered by gradient coupling, barren plateaus, data-loading bottlenecks, and high inference latency. To bridge classical AI and QML, we propose QPAT (QCBM-Prior-Assisted Training), a universal framework that employs a Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) as a learnable generative prior to provide a task-aligned structured inductive bias during classical model training. The framework can be seamlessly integrated into any classical backbone, including LSTMs, CNNs, and Transformers. We introduce a decoupled fitness-based scoring mechanism and a stochastic "Drop-Prior" mechanism to implicitly distill quantum structural knowledge into the classical weights during training. Evaluated extensively on six benchmarks spanning time-series forecasting, computer vision, and natural language processing, our framework consistently outperforms purely classical backbones in both predictive performance and stability across random seeds; ablation studies further show that these gains are not reproduced by unstructured random priors or a classically learned generative prior. Remarkably, our approach enables completely classical inference, bypassing quantum latency while preserving quantum-enhanced accuracy, paving a highly practical path for QML deployment.

item.title: A bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs based on beam-like Type-II SPDC
item.description: arXiv:2611.33852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bright sources of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs are increasingly required for the rapid advancement of quantum technologies. However, simultaneously achieving high brightness and high-dimensional spatial entangle…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bright sources of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs are increasingly required for the rapid advancement of quantum technologies. However, simultaneously achieving high brightness and high-dimensional spatial entanglement through spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs using beam-like Type-II SPDC in a $\beta$-barium borate crystal. Compared with a conventional collinear Type-I source, it exhibits a $\sim$1.56-fold enhancement in the detected single-photon count rate and a $\sim$1.45-fold enhancement in the coincidence count rate. Measurements of position correlations and momentum anti-correlations certify at least 62-dimensional spatial entanglement within a 121-dimensional basis. These correlations are further exploited to demonstrate quantum imaging in both the position and momentum domains. These characteristics make the source a practical resource for high-dimensional photonic quantum technologies.

item.title: Efficient Quantum Algorithm for the Generalised Geography Game
item.description: arXiv:2611.33853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Generalized Geography Game ($GGG$) is a two-player combinatorial game played on a directed graph, where players alternately move a token along edges without revisiting previously visited vertices. In the existing literature, det…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Generalized Geography Game ($GGG$) is a two-player combinatorial game played on a directed graph, where players alternately move a token along edges without revisiting previously visited vertices. In the existing literature, determining whether an arbitrary position in a graph is a winning position for either player is a well-known $PSPACE$-complete decision problem. Certain formulations of $GGG$ have been shown to fall outside the $PSPACE$-complete complexity class. While $PSPACE$-complete problems are believed to take exponential time for classical computation, quantum computation offers new possibilities. In this work, we present a bounded-error quantum polynomial-time ($BQP$) algorithm for solving the $GGG$ problem. The proposed algorithm runs in time $O(N^{2}/\epsilon^{6})$, which is polynomial in the input size $N$, and achieves bounded error with $\epsilon = O(1/\mathrm{poly}(N))$. This result demonstrates the potential of quantum algorithms to efficiently solve combinatorial game problems that are traditionally considered computationally hard in the classical setting.

item.title: Reproducible distributions of energy-relaxation times in superconducting qubits from broadband SWAP spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.33854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The distribution of the qubit energy-relaxation time (T1) in a superconducting quantum processor affects its logical error rates. However, reports on qubit fabrication quality focus on the median or best-case T1 from measurements th…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The distribution of the qubit energy-relaxation time (T1) in a superconducting quantum processor affects its logical error rates. However, reports on qubit fabrication quality focus on the median or best-case T1 from measurements that are not reproducible due to resonant coupling to two-level system (TLS) defects whose frequencies fluctuate in time. Here, we sweep the frequency f01 of a flux-tunable qubit over several GHz with SWAP spectroscopy, quoting the quality factor Q = 2 pi f01 T1 to make T1 comparable across frequencies. We show that the cumulative distribution of Q pooled over the sweep is reproducible across four thermal cycles spanning 326 days, up to the reshuffling of strongly coupled TLSs. In contrast to repeated measurements at a single frequency, the medians of the broadband Q distributions spread by an order of magnitude less over 3 days. The distance between the cumulative distributions of repeats comes close to its sampling floor only for the broadband sweeps. The broadband Q distribution further resolves small coherence differences between identically designed qubits on two dies of the same wafer. These results establish the broadband Q distribution as a reproducible metric for qubit fabrication quality.

item.description: arXiv:2611.33864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Depolarizing noise scales trace distances by a common factor. An encoded qubit is autonomous if its reduced input state determines its output. For $D=2^n\ge4$, autonomy forces this isotropy at a sharp threshold of $(D^2+5)/3$ generi…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Depolarizing noise scales trace distances by a common factor. An encoded qubit is autonomous if its reduced input state determines its output. For $D=2^n\ge4$, autonomy forces this isotropy at a sharp threshold of $(D^2+5)/3$ generic encodings, two more than state tomography requires. For Pauli noise, one generic encoding suffices. With one-bit readouts and no quantum memory or reference, switching encodings cuts the worst-case cost for the Pauli test by a factor of $D$, up to logarithms. For any family, a channel with leakage $O(D^{-3/2})$ can transmit one bit perfectly and erase another.

item.title: Decoherent Histories from Local Spectral Dephasing in Quantum Many-Body Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.33888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study local spectral dephasing as a mechanism for decoherent histories in isolated quantum many-body systems. We prove that vanishing projector-weighted spectral concentration is asymptotically equivalent to vanishing time-averag…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study local spectral dephasing as a mechanism for decoherent histories in isolated quantum many-body systems. We prove that vanishing projector-weighted spectral concentration is asymptotically equivalent to vanishing time-averaged local memory. With independently sampled waiting times and suitable conditions on the initial state and history weights, this local property suppresses normalized interference across complete fixed-length history families with high probability. For translation-invariant lattices, spectral estimates provide conditions under which dephasing occurs at long times. Exact diagonalization and sparse time evolution of a spin chain illustrate the results.

item.title: Phonon-Aware Electron-to-Nuclear Spin Quantum Memory in NV Centers
item.description: arXiv:2611.33936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a promising solid-state platform for quantum memory: the electron spin can be optically initialized and read out, while nearby nuclear spins have long coherence times and can serve as sto…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a promising solid-state platform for quantum memory: the electron spin can be optically initialized and read out, while nearby nuclear spins have long coherence times and can serve as storage qubits. In this work, we develop a phonon-aware open quantum system model for electron-to-nuclear spin state transfer in a single NV center. The model includes the NV electron spin, a coupled 13C nuclear spin, the hyperfine interaction, an effective microwave/radio-frequency-assisted SWAP interaction for writing and reading, a single effective phonon mode with longitudinal spin-phonon coupling, and Lindblad relaxation and dephasing channels. The dynamics are simulated with the Lindblad master equation in QuTiP, using the secular approximation and a hyperfine-resonant drive in the rotating frame. Without spin-phonon coupling and electron decoherence, the write-store-read protocol recovers the stored state with a fidelity above 0.9999. With the default decoherence rates, increasing the spin-phonon coupling from 0 to 0.06 MHz lowers the worst-case retrieval fidelity from 0.9994 to 0.9884, and the fidelity oscillates with the phonon-mode period because electron-phonon entanglement generated during the write step is partially undone during the read step. With a phenomenological temperature-dependent rate model, the fidelity decreases monotonically from 0.9997 at 1 K to 0.9938 at 300 K, while storage-time losses follow the assumed nuclear-spin decoherence rates. The storage-time plots, temperature sweep, and parameter maps identify operating regimes for NV-center quantum memory, and the accompanying open-source code provides a reproducible framework for studying phonon-limited quantum memory.

item.title: Empirical De-Quantization and Norm-Controlled Spectral Audit of Quantum Cognition Machine Learning in an Emerging Equity Market
item.description: arXiv:2611.33942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum-inspired machine learning in econophysics describes states of financial markets through matrix Hamiltonians, using ground-state expectations to predict returns and spectral gaps to identify crises. Although early work report…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum-inspired machine learning in econophysics describes states of financial markets through matrix Hamiltonians, using ground-state expectations to predict returns and spectral gaps to identify crises. Although early work reports encouraging advances, it remains unclear whether these stem from genuine noncommutative quantum geometry or from conventional classical regularization and scale effects. We test this in a controlled audit of matrix-form Quantum Cognition Machine Learning (QCML) and variational quantum circuits on the Moscow Exchange (2020-2025), combining daily equity data with causally lagged macro news under realistic trading costs, short-selling bans, and abrupt shifts in market regimes. By using capacity-matched operator swaps -- which progressively eliminate complex Berry phases and matrix noncommutativity down to a commuting classical Gibbs radial-basis limit under scale-invariant regularization -- as well as testing spectral indicators against radial-norm null hypotheses and untrained GUE random matrices, we isolate the contribution of each quantum element. In out-of-sample data, neither complex phases, noncommutativity, nor circuit entanglement improves the ranking of returns relative to classical controls. Once feature magnitudes are normalized, apparent crisis detection from raw spectral gaps drops below chance levels. These results show that on noisy equity panels, matrix-form QCML acts as an adaptive spectrally bounded classical smoothing kernel: it reliably integrates lagged news and curbs extreme crisis forecasts without passing economic multiple-testing thresholds, while our audit provides operator-swap and random-matrix controls for evaluating future quantum-inspired financial models.

item.title: Gaussian Is All You Need: Renyi Optimizers and Optical Channel Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.33955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Preparing an entangled state faithfully requires an amount of resource given by its entanglement cost. With less entanglement, the best achievable fidelity is governed by the R\'enyi entanglement of formation of orders above one. We…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Preparing an entangled state faithfully requires an amount of resource given by its entanglement cost. With less entanglement, the best achievable fidelity is governed by the R\'enyi entanglement of formation of orders above one. We prove that, for any finite-energy multimode bosonic Gaussian state, all these quantities are additive and attained by a Gaussian pure-state decomposition. It follows that the closest separable state in fidelity to any Gaussian state is Gaussian, and that the strong converse exponent of entanglement dilution, which sets how fast the optimal fidelity decays below the cost, is exactly computable. For channels, we prove that pure Gaussian inputs minimize the output R\'enyi entropies of every multimode Gaussian channel at all orders $\alpha\ge1$, and we obtain the optimal fidelity of simulating pure-loss and quantum-limited amplifier channels with finite entanglement, for any number of uses.

item.title: Discrete truncated Wigner approximation of the quantum phase transition in the transverse-field Ising model
item.description: arXiv:2611.34004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The discrete truncated Wigner approximation (DTWA) has been a workhorse for large-scale spin dynamics, but whether it captures dynamics across a quantum phase transition has not been tested systematically. In this work, we use the t…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.34004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The discrete truncated Wigner approximation (DTWA) has been a workhorse for large-scale spin dynamics, but whether it captures dynamics across a quantum phase transition has not been tested systematically. In this work, we use the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) to study the quantum phase transition with DTWA from one to three dimensions and with all-to-all connectivity, using slow linear ramps and fast ramps. We find that DTWA cannot capture the dynamics on the one-dimensional chain, and that its behavior is consistent with classical thermalization, in which its classical spins relax toward a thermal state at a finite effective temperature that does not vanish for slow ramps, while a one-dimensional chain cannot order at any finite temperature. For square and cubic lattices, in contrast to the chain, DTWA builds order, and the order sets in close to the quantum critical point found by quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). However, its correlations do not grow with the Kibble-Zurek exponents, so DTWA captures the onset of order but not the universal dynamics of the transition. For all-to-all coupling, DTWA follows the exact growth of the order parameter along the entire ramp. Our results suggest that DTWA becomes more reliable as each spin interacts with more partners, and that beyond one dimension it can indicate where a quantum phase transition lies but cannot capture its critical scaling.

item.title: Quantum Advantage in Privacy-Preserving Hypothesis Testing via Entanglement-Assisted Classical Communication
item.description: arXiv:2611.34029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum mechanisms satisfying quantum local differential privacy (QLDP) have been shown to achieve a quantum advantage over classical local differential privacy (LDP) mechanisms in certain hypothesis-testing problems. While previous…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.34029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum mechanisms satisfying quantum local differential privacy (QLDP) have been shown to achieve a quantum advantage over classical local differential privacy (LDP) mechanisms in certain hypothesis-testing problems. While previous demonstrations have considered the transmission of quantum states from users to a server, we investigate whether this advantage can persist under entanglement-assisted classical communication (EACC), where users and the server share entanglement in advance and communicate only classical messages. We formulate an EACC-based hypothesis-testing framework and introduce measurement local differential privacy (MLDP) to protect private inputs against arbitrary shared quantum states and server-side measurements. We establish that QLDP classical-to-quantum channels admit MLDP-compliant EACC simulations and that, in the high-privacy regime, certain optimal QLDP mechanisms can be realized with one-bit classical communication, albeit using high-dimensional entanglement. We then demonstrate that a strict quantum advantage persists even when the pre-shared entanglement is restricted to a single qubit pair and each user communicates only one classical bit. Using EACC protocols based on the geometry of qubit measurements, we establish this advantage for both asymmetric and symmetric hypothesis testing and every input alphabet of size $v \geq 3$ in the high-privacy limit. The ratio of the achieved error exponent to the optimal one under the LDP constraint is at least $5/4$ for all such alphabets and approaches $3/2$ as $v$ grows. These results demonstrate that quantum advantage in locally private hypothesis testing can persist under simultaneous constraints on entanglement dimension and classical communication.

item.title: Schism: Reconfigurable Scale-Up Domains for Distributed Quantum Computing
item.description: arXiv:2611.31193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Switch-based quantum datacenters connect quantum processing units (QPUs) through photonic switches and shared Bell-state measurement (BSM) devices. Sharing BSMs saves hardware, but fixed connectivity constrains access to these res…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.31193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Switch-based quantum datacenters connect quantum processing units (QPUs) through photonic switches and shared Bell-state measurement (BSM) devices. Sharing BSMs saves hardware, but fixed connectivity constrains access to these resources. Local communication can overload one rack's BSMs while others remain idle; reaching those idle resources incurs additional optical loss and retries through switches and quantum frequency converters (QFCs). Programs remain locked into this locality-contention tradeoff as their communication patterns change. We propose Schism, an architecture that lets programs dynamically change which QPUs share each BSM pool. Schism places BSM pools at aggregation switches and QFCs on their core-facing uplinks. Top-of-rack switches establish reconfigurable native-wavelength circuits from QPUs to these pools, forming scale-up domains bounded by the optical loss budget. Reconfiguration reshapes resource sharing across racks without moving QPUs or migrating quantum states. Our key insight is that QPU grouping jointly determines photon-path loss and contention for BSM resources: locality alone cannot identify the best grouping, and a grouping pays off only if its savings outweigh the delay of reconfiguring to it. We develop an optimization framework that combines graph partitioning with resource-constrained completion-time estimates and dynamic programming to select how QPUs share BSM pools and when those groupings reconfigure, between or within circuit phases. Our evaluation using SeQUeNCe with trapped-ion parameters shows that Schism achieves communication speedups of 4.9-7.3x across 11 workloads on 32 QPUs compared to Fixed Clos connectivity and 3.6-8.3x compared to SwitchQNet. Schism also outperforms a hypothetical network-wide switch by 1.35-1.38x on the eight workloads whose phases fit in a pool, and trails it by 1.1-1.75x on the other three.

item.title: A novel quantum lattice Boltzmann methodology for cosmological radiation transport
item.description: arXiv:2611.31340v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Radiation transport is an essential process in many physical simulations, including cosmological codes which track stellar and diffuse radiation. Many present codes utilize ray tracing or moment methods, but these grow increasingl…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.31340v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Radiation transport is an essential process in many physical simulations, including cosmological codes which track stellar and diffuse radiation. Many present codes utilize ray tracing or moment methods, but these grow increasingly difficult and expensive for large simulations. Quantum lattice Boltzmann methods exponentially reduce complexity by propagating radiation over a lattice, allowing for better spatial resolution without needing to introduce adaptive ray tracing or other optimizations. However, existing formulations result in poor angular resolution for radiation point sources. In this work, we propose an angular redistribution methodology which significantly improves the resolution with minimal increase in complexity. We verify the correctness of the method on both classical processors and quantum simulators and outline how the quantum algorithm can be integrated into existing codes. This method is an important step towards fully-quantum radiation hydrodynamics simulation which could exponentially accelerate existing cosmological codes, enabling simulations at scales currently infeasible.

item.title: Theory of Anomalous Diffusion and Superdiffusion in Integrable Spin Chains
item.description: arXiv:2611.33274v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrable systems can exhibit diffusive or Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) scaling in two-point correlations even when their current full counting statistics (FCS) differ from those usually associated with these universality classes.…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33274v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrable systems can exhibit diffusive or Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) scaling in two-point correlations even when their current full counting statistics (FCS) differ from those usually associated with these universality classes. We explain this separation using a multispecies particle gas that preserves the scattering structure of integrable spin chains. For anisotropy $\Delta>1$, large particles are advected by a mobile bath. The resulting FCS has a Gaussian-mixture form and approaches the M-Wright distribution at late times, with finite-time rounding due to mobile species. At the isotropic point $\Delta=1$, all particles are mobile, and the charge transfer by large particles is discrete. A self-consistent Poisson distribution describes the FCS, with a nearly Gaussian bulk and model-dependent, non-Gaussian tails. By contrast, two-point correlations follow from the statistics of a large tracer particle. For $\Delta>1$, it undergoes Brownian motion, yielding Gaussian spreading. At $\Delta=1$, we provide evidence from fluctuating hydrodynamics for the emergence of the KPZ Pr\"ahofer--Spohn scaling function in dynamical correlations and trace it to the finite coupling of the largest particles to a continuum of slower ones, with long-ranged velocity fluctuations. Our framework shows how universal dynamical two-point correlations coexist with distinct model-dependent current statistics.

item.title: Parton structure of mesonic states with tensor networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.33280v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the first direct tensor network calculation of flavor-resolved parton distribution functions (PDFs) for a pion-like isospin triplet in the two-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model in (1+1) dimensions. Four-fermion interactio…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33280v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the first direct tensor network calculation of flavor-resolved parton distribution functions (PDFs) for a pion-like isospin triplet in the two-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model in (1+1) dimensions. Four-fermion interactions bind the mesons without confinement. Using staggered fermions and a charge-symmetrized Hamiltonian, we prepare the bound states and compute light-cone correlators by real-time evolution. The resulting quark and antiquark PDFs obey the expected isospin relations under $u \leftrightarrow d$ exchange between charged pions and exhibit equal u and d distributions in the neutral pion. A flavor-independent antisymmetrization of the field ordering removes the vacuum-subtracted anticommutator contribution and restores charge-conjugation relations in both the correlators and PDFs across the triplet within numerical accuracy. These results provide benchmarks for quantum simulations of the partonic structure of the meson.

item.title: Energy plateau cascades from complex-time local quenches in thermal two-dimensional CFTs
item.description: arXiv:2611.33283v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we study local operator quenches in thermal two-dimensional conformal field theories with complex-time evolution, which can be viewed as an effective description of conditional dynamics in a system interacting with a…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33283v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we study local operator quenches in thermal two-dimensional conformal field theories with complex-time evolution, which can be viewed as an effective description of conditional dynamics in a system interacting with an environment. In contrast to quenches of the vacuum, the thermal initial state allows several conformal families to participate in the evolution. We show that their competition can produce cascades of approximately homogeneous energy plateaux, with successive plateaux approaching the energies of different primary states. Using conformal Ward identities on the cylinder and torus, we determine the local energy density and illustrate this behavior in free-field theories, the Ising model and Wess--Zumino--Witten models. We develop a cold-limit spectral description in which the dominant primary channel determines the height of each plateau, while conformal dimensions and operator matrix elements govern the transitions between them. For a fixed compact unitary CFT, we show that only finitely many primary channels can contribute to the leading plateau sequence. Finally, we discuss the large-central-charge regime, relating light-operator plateaux to few-particle sectors in thermal AdS and examining the limitations of this picture for heavy quenches.

item.title: Bosonic Magic Resources at Quantum Criticality
item.description: arXiv:2611.33306v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Non-Gaussianity is a resource for bosonic quantum information processing, providing a necessary ingredient for universal quantum computation in continuous-variable systems. Here we quantify non-Gaussianity in the ground state of t…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33306v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Non-Gaussianity is a resource for bosonic quantum information processing, providing a necessary ingredient for universal quantum computation in continuous-variable systems. Here we quantify non-Gaussianity in the ground state of the one-dimensional extended Bose-Hubbard model using quantum relative entropy (QRE), a measure determined solely by one-body correlations. The scaling of the QRE with system size reveals quantum phase transitions involving hidden and conventional order. We connect QRE scaling in the weakly interacting superfluid phase to Luttinger-liquid correlations and identify distinct critical signatures in its extensive and subleading contributions. At the Mott-Haldane transition, subtracting the extensive background reveals a pronounced peak in the subleading contribution, providing a clear signature of the onset of hidden string order. At the Haldane-density-wave transition, the extensive contribution to the QRE instead exhibits scaling consistent with Ising criticality. These results establish non-Gaussianity as a probe of many-body criticality, linking bosonic quantum resources to strongly correlated matter.

item.title: Modular fluctuation relations on local causal horizons
item.description: arXiv:2611.33384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local causal horizons provide a setting for studying horizon thermodynamics in the neighborhood of any regular spacetime point. Here, we investigate this description beyond mean energy and entropy balances by studying fluctuations…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local causal horizons provide a setting for studying horizon thermodynamics in the neighborhood of any regular spacetime point. Here, we investigate this description beyond mean energy and entropy balances by studying fluctuations of boost-energy transfer induced by unitary perturbations of the horizon reference state. Using the modular structure of the horizon algebra and a thermal reference state, we construct an energy transfer probability measure and derive integral and detailed fluctuation relations with the mean entropy production being expressed in terms of the Araki relative entropy. The formulation accommodates type-III algebras without introducing a reduced density matrix and can be extended to global bifurcate Killing horizons admitting the required thermal reference state. For coherent scalar-field perturbations, we obtain a closed form for the characteristic function, identify the mean transfer with the excess boost-energy flux, and derive a thermodynamic uncertainty relation bounding the variance in terms of the mean transfer. We then explore the geometric implications by postulating a stochastic horizon entropy--area correspondence that associates an area change with each counted energy transfer. Under this additional hypothesis, we obtain fluctuation relations for area changes and an area change uncertainty bound for coherent perturbations.

item.title: Superconductivity from the Berry connection from many-electron wave functions: $U(1)$ gauge fluctuation, gauge invariance, and superconductivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.33723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The electromagnetic $U(1)$ gauge invariance and superconductivity are examined by employing the Berry connection from many-electron wave functions and the fluctuations of it that give rise to the probabilistic random transitions a…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.33723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The electromagnetic $U(1)$ gauge invariance and superconductivity are examined by employing the Berry connection from many-electron wave functions and the fluctuations of it that give rise to the probabilistic random transitions among quantum states. The gauge invariance in the classical electrodynamics is regarded as the requirement that extracts unaffected parts by the gauge fluctuation. In quantum mechanics, dissipation-free states from the gauge fluctuation exist, and we identify them as superconducting states. We explain the reversible superconducting-normal phase transition in a magnetic field including the force balance. The present superconductivity theory lifts two fundamental disagreements between theory and experiment existing in the current standard theory with keeping the major results by the BCS theory. Thus, it may be considered as a superconductivity theory encompassing the current standard one.
